risks.risk: Unknown UPS capacity (VA/W) and battery size; runtime depends heavily on load and battery capacity.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the rating label showing VA/W and battery voltage/capacity (e.g., 12V/24V and Ah) on the back/bottom.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as a generic used UPS with unknown capacity; treat as worst-case for runtime (not guaranteed 8 hours).

risks.risk: Battery health may be degraded even if it “charges”; the 8-hour claim could be under a very light load.
risks.proof: A video showing a full charge test: UPS on battery mode with a stated load (watts) and timer reaching the claimed duration.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as not proven to reach 8 hours; assume reduced runtime.

risks.risk: Whether the UPS switches to battery correctly and whether the inverter output is stable (voltage waveform/AVR issues).
risks.proof: A short clip showing: mains off → UPS switches to battery (beep/LED change), and a multimeter reading of output voltage under load.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as not fully verified for correct switching/output quality.

risks.risk: Possible prior repair or battery replacement quality (non-original cells, poor connections) not visible externally.
risks.proof: Photo of the inside (battery compartment) or a clear view of any warranty/service seals and the battery label.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as potentially repaired/unknown battery quality until proven otherwise.

risks.risk: Missing accessories/cables (e.g., manual, proper power cable) or damaged ports.
risks.proof: Photo of all included items and close-ups of ports/connectors on the back/top.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as sold as-is with only what’s shown; assume missing items/unknown condition.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the UPS rating label (VA/W) and battery specs (voltage and Ah) on the back/bottom.
Video test: charge to full, then mains off with a stated load (watts) and timer to show runtime.
Video showing battery-mode switching and output voltage reading (multimeter) under load.
Photo of battery compartment/inside or any battery label + any warranty/service seal.
response.reason: The photos confirm it’s a BLUE GATE UPS, but the key pricing drivers (capacity/VA, battery Ah, and verified runtime under load) are not visible, so a worst-case price can’t be set confidently without the missing labels and test proof.
